memory_update.text: WCC should be retained as a reference distributor for the consumer infrastructure power stack, but not treated as the main alpha-hunting name because its market cap is above the preferred 300M-10B range.

ATKR is a strong underfollowed Layer 1B candidate for conduit, cable-management, metal framing, and wiring-protection products tied to commercial renovation, warehouses, EV charging, and electrification.
MYRG maps to field-labor and electrical-construction capacity, a possible chokepoint if commercial load growth requires more substations, distribution work, and complex C&I installation.
LMB is a small-cap retrofit/service candidate for building-level MEPC systems and controls, but consumer-specific exposure must be verified before it can survive later funnel layers.

Current evidence generally supports electrical-infrastructure relevance, but not yet direct revenue attribution to retail, hospitality, food service, cold chain, or ecommerce fulfillment customers. Later layers should require end-market mix, named projects, backlog detail, or customer case studies.

The most actionable subnodes appear to be electrical distribution, conduit/cable management, specialty electrical contracting, and owner-direct building-system retrofits rather than only headline switchgear and transformer OEMs.

node: Electrical infrastructure for consumer-facing physical assets: stores, warehouses, cold chain, hotels, restaurants, and fulfillment centers
summary: Expanded the underfollowed universe around consumer-facing electrical infrastructure one layer below headline power demand. The pass avoids mega-cap electrical OEMs except as context and prioritizes distributors, field labor, conduit/cable-management suppliers, and building-systems service firms that can benefit when stores, warehouses, hospitality assets, restaurants, cold-chain nodes, and fulfillment centers add electrical load, controls, backup power, EV charging, automation, and data-heavy systems. Key caveat: most exposures are not reported as clean 'consumer infrastructure' revenue lines, so these names enter Layer 1B as evidence-backed hypotheses requiring customer/end-market verification.
